multiNicHelpHint: Click to see when this helps
multiNicHelp:
How it works: the segment connections of one file are bound to different network adapters, so several internet lines fetch data at the same time and their speeds add up.

When it helps: each adapter leads to a different upstream line (home broadband + 5G hotspot, two carriers, or two broadband lines), and the bottleneck is your own uplink bandwidth. When a server rate-limits per IP, each exit also gets its own quota.

When it doesn't: Ethernet and Wi‑Fi on the same router (the same broadband line) share the same bottleneck, so aggregation gains nothing — the engine detects the shared LAN and ignores the duplicate adapter automatically. It also won't help when the server itself lacks bandwidth or limits speed per connection.

How it avoids slowing you down: each adapter is first measured with one real segment connection, then connections are allocated by measured throughput. A slow line only gets work proportional to its capacity, the tail is split by speed ratio, and stalled connections are handed over to other lines immediately. If no usable extra line is found, behavior is exactly the same as with this feature off.

When it stays off: the task uses a proxy, a VPN/TUN virtual adapter is carrying the traffic, the download address is on the local network, or the server doesn't support segmented downloads.

Note: going through a phone hotspot uses cellular data. A few signed links or cloud drives bound to the source IP may reject requests from another exit; a failing adapter is removed from that task. Once enabled, per-adapter connection counts and downloaded bytes appear in the task details "Log" tab.

autoRetryCountDesc: Number of automatic retries after transient errors (e.g. network drops)
autoRetryDelayDesc: Seconds to wait before each auto-retry (increases per attempt)
proxySettingsDesc: Proxy for HTTP/FTP/HLS downloads, RSS and plugin requests
proxyManualKeptDesc: Not used as the global proxy in the current mode, but your entries are kept and still used by Auto mode as an alternative path, and by site rules and tasks set to Manual proxy.
proxyModeAutoDesc: Starts direct without blocking and treats every available manual and system proxy as a parallel path. Each path is measured with real segments whose bytes go straight into the file, connections flow to the faster path, slow connections hand off at the current byte, and direct and proxy can be combined. Direct still keeps multi-CDN acceleration.
proxyConfigureInSettings: Configure a proxy in Settings first
proxyNoListDesc: Addresses that bypass proxy, comma separated
proxyBtNote: BitTorrent and eD2K peer connections never use a proxy
proxyRulesDesc: Send specific sites through a chosen exit. Rules take priority over the proxy mode above, including No Proxy and Auto, and the first matching rule from the top wins.
proxyRulesScope: Applies to HTTP/HTTPS, FTP and HLS/DASH downloads (including redirects and segments), RSS feeds, plugin requests, and FluxDown's own downloads such as updates, components and plugin packages. Tasks and feeds with their own proxy, and webhook deliveries, are not affected.
proxyRulesActiveHint: {count} site rule(s) take priority over this mode
proxyRulesEmptyDesc: For example, send github.com through your proxy and keep an intranet mirror direct.
proxyRuleDeleteDesc: Matching links will follow the proxy mode again.
proxyRulePatternDomainHint: Separate multiple domains with commas or spaces. Subdomains are included: github.com also matches api.github.com.
proxyRulePatternRegexHint: Matched against the full URL (scheme, host, path and query), case-insensitive, anywhere in the URL. Uses Rust regex syntax, which has no lookaround or backreferences.
proxyRuleActionSystemHint: Use the proxy server set in the operating system of the download host, or connect directly if none is set. PAC scripts are not run. When the download host runs on Android or iOS, the system proxy can't be read, so this means direct.
proxyRuleActionManualHint: Uses the server from Manual configuration: {endpoint}
proxyRuleActionManualMissing: No manual proxy server is set yet; matching links will connect directly.
proxyRuleProxyUrlHint: http, https, socks4, socks4a, socks5 or socks5h, with optional credentials: socks5://user:pass@host:port
proxyRouteTestDesc: See which exit a URL would use with the saved rules and the current mode.
proxyRouteBypass: Direct, listed in the bypass list
proxyRouteModePac: Decided by the system PAC script at download time
proxyRouteModeAuto: Auto: starts direct and races the configured proxies
proxyRouteUnsupported: This kind of link never uses a proxy
proxyRouteInvalidUrl: Enter a full URL, such as https://example.com/file.zip
proxyTestTlsEndpointHint: The proxy endpoint did not accept a TLS handshake. If this is a mixed HTTP/SOCKS port (Clash, V2Ray) or a plain HTTP proxy, select the HTTP type instead of HTTPS.
userAgentDesc: Browser identity used in download requests.
userAgentPlaceholder: Leave empty for default identity FluxDown/<version>
userAgentTaskPlaceholder: Leave empty to use global setting
revealFileCmdDesc: Third-party file manager command used to open files/folders. Placeholders: {path} = current path (a downloaded file uses its full path — most managers locate and select it; for a directory it is the folder path), {dir} = directory (parent dir for files). Leave empty to use the platform default (Explorer / Finder / Nautilus, etc.).
taskProxyDesc: Follow Global uses the proxy mode and site rules; any other choice ignores site rules for this task
taskProxyFormatHint:
Supported proxy formats:

Without auth:
  http://host:port
  socks5://host:port

With username & password:
  http://user:pass@host:port
  socks5://user:pass@host:port

Supported types: http / https / socks4 / socks5
Leave empty to use global proxy settings
taskIgnoreTlsErrorsDesc: Allows expired, self-signed, or mismatched certificates for this task only. This may expose the download to interception.
taskCookieDesc: Used for downloads requiring login (empty = none)
taskCookieBatchDesc: Batch: empty = each item keeps its own captured cookies; filled = overrides all
taskChecksumDesc: Verify file integrity after download (empty = skip)
taskHeadersDesc: Add extra HTTP headers for this task (use the Cookie field above for cookies)
taskHttpAuthDesc: HTTP Basic credentials for this site. Leave empty to reuse credentials saved for this site. Saved credentials are stored locally in plain text
settingsSiteAuthDesc: HTTP authentication credentials saved per site, stored on this device only and applied automatically to new downloads
apiServiceEnableDesc: Start the local HTTP API service (127.0.0.1 only) used by the feature toggles below
apiServicePortFixed: The listening address is fixed by the startup environment and cannot be changed here.
apiServicePortRestartHint: Changing the port automatically restarts the API service. If startup verification fails, the previous service and port are kept.
apiServiceRestarted: API service restarted successfully on port {port}.
apiServicePortInUse: That port is already in use. The API service is still running on the previous port.
apiServiceRestartFailed: The API service could not restart or pass startup verification. The previous service and port have been kept.
apiServiceTokenDesc: Access token for API requests; type your own or click Generate for a random one. Required once the management API is enabled
apiServiceTokenClearConfirmDesc: The management API is enabled and depends on this token. Clearing it will also turn off the management API. Continue?
apiServiceFeaturesDesc: Control which API surface each module exposes (disabled when the master switch is off)
apiServiceTakeoverDesc: Lets the FluxDown userscript take over browser downloads
apiServiceUserscriptDesc: Copy a ready-to-use script with the active port and access token. Uses the browser capture endpoint; CORS can stay off. Do not share the script; copy it again after changing the port or token.
apiServiceScriptCopied: Script copied; paste it into a new Tampermonkey script
apiServiceJsonrpcDesc: Implements the aria2 JSON-RPC protocol for "send to aria2" scripts or clients like AriaNg
apiServiceApiDesc: HTTP API for querying and controlling tasks, for MCP servers and automation scripts (authentication required)
apiServiceMcpDesc: Exposes a Model Context Protocol endpoint for AI clients like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Cline (shares the Management API token, authentication required)
apiServiceHostNone: No active network interface detected. Only the loopback address is available.
btEnabledDesc: Enable BitTorrent downloads, peer discovery, and listening
btEnableDhtDesc: Distributed Hash Table for trackerless peer discovery
btEnableUpnpDesc: Auto-configure router port forwarding for better connectivity
btEnableUtpDesc: Also connect to peers over uTP (UDP) to reach more peers behind NAT; uses more CPU than TCP
btPieceOrderDesc: The order new BT tasks download pieces in. Applies to tasks added from now on; change a single task from its context menu
btPieceOrderRarestDesc: Download first the pieces the fewest connected peers have (default).
btPieceOrderSequentialDesc: Download pieces in file order, files sorted by name.
btFirstLastPiecesFirstDefault: Download First and Last Pieces First
btFirstLastPiecesFirstDefaultDesc: New BT tasks download the first and last 1% of every selected file (at least one piece each) before the rest. Applies to tasks added from now on; change a single task from its context menu
btListenPortDesc: Port range for incoming BT connections
btTrackerListDesc: Trackers automatically added to new BT tasks, one URL per line. Changes apply immediately and don't affect running tasks
btTrackerPlaceholder:
One tracker URL per line, e.g.:
udp://tracker.opentrackr.org:1337/announce
https://tracker.example.com/announce
btTrackerSubDesc: Periodically fetch up-to-date trackers from community-maintained lists, merged and deduplicated with the list above
btTrackerSubPlaceholder:
One subscription URL per line, e.g.:
https://trackerslist.com/best.txt
https://ngosang.github.io/trackerslist/trackers_best.txt
btTrackerSubUrlsDesc: Tracker list URLs to subscribe to, one per line; lines starting with # are ignored
ed2kSettingsDesc: Configure eD2K servers and server.met subscription
ed2kServerListDesc: Manually configured eD2K servers (for finding sources), merged and deduplicated with the subscription list
ed2kServerSubDesc: Periodically fetch up-to-date servers from community-maintained server.met lists, merged and deduplicated with the list above
ed2kEnableKadDesc: Find sources via the decentralized Kad network, works even when all servers are down
ed2kEnableUpnpDesc: Auto-map ports via UPnP to obtain HighID, connecting to more peers and receiving callbacks
ed2kListenPortDesc: eD2K client TCP/UDP listen port (0 = auto-select)
ed2kServerSubPlaceholder:
One server.met URL per line, e.g.:
https://upd.emule-security.org/server.met
https://www.shortypower.org/server.met
ed2kServerSubUrlsDesc: server.met URLs to subscribe to, one per line; ed2k://|serverlist|…|/ links are supported

filePickerErrorNoTool:

Install xdg-desktop-portal-gtk (recommended) or zenity / kdialog:
sudo pacman -S xdg-desktop-portal-gtk or sudo apt install xdg-desktop-portal-gtk
filePickerErrorNative: Failed to open file picker dialog, please try again.
filePickerErrorGeneric: Failed to open file picker, please try again.
btSettingsRestartHint: Changing port, DHT, UPnP, uTP or encryption settings rebuilds the BT engine automatically; running downloads and seeds carry on
autoCheckUpdateDesc: Automatically check for updates on startup
updateChannelDesc: Frontier delivers preview builds ahead of stable — may be unstable
donateBody: Since {date}, FluxDown has shipped {releases} releases with over {commits} commits — always free, with zero ads and zero tracking. Ongoing development relies on your support and feedback.
donateThanks: Your support helps FluxDown keep improving. Thank you so much!
extensionCardDesc: Install the browser extension or userscript to intercept browser downloads and send them to FluxDown. Supports Chrome, Edge, Firefox and other Chromium-based browsers.
updatePromptBody: Version v{v} is available ({size}). Update now?
updateFallbackTaskCreated: Added the update to the download list
autoCheckUpdateBackgroundDesc: Check for updates in the background and download them automatically, so updating only takes a restart
updateReadyToast: FluxDown v{v} is ready. Restart to finish updating.
updateInstalling: Installing the update. FluxDown will restart…
updateInstalledToast: FluxDown has been updated to v{v}.
updateRestartingBody: The service is restarting with the new version. This page reloads automatically when it is back.
updateManualDocker: Running in Docker: pull the new image and recreate the container (docker pull ghcr.io/zerx-lab/fluxdown-server:latest).
updateManualSynology: Installed from Synology Package Center: update FluxDown there or install the new .spk package manually.
updateManualQnap: Installed from QNAP App Center: update FluxDown there or install the new .qpkg package manually.
updateManualOpenwrt: Installed with the OpenWrt package manager: install the new .ipk (opkg) or .apk (apk) package to update.
updateManualFnos: Installed from the fnOS App Center: install the new .fpk package to update.
updateManualSystemPackage: Installed by your system package manager (e.g. from the AUR or a distribution repository): update FluxDown with that package manager, e.g. yay -Syu or paru -Syu for the AUR.
updateManualNotWritable: FluxDown's folder is not writable, so it can't update itself. Move it to a writable folder or download the update manually.
updateManualNoAsset: No update package is published for this system yet. Download the update manually.
updateManualElevation: Installing this package needs administrator rights, but no graphical authorization prompt is available. Install the update with your package manager.
updateManualReadOnly: FluxDown is running from a read-only copy (macOS randomizes the path of quarantined apps, or the app is running from a disk image). Quit FluxDown, run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/FluxDown.app in Terminal (or drag the app out of Applications and back in Finder), then reopen it and update.
updateManualUnofficial: This is not an official signed build, so it can't update itself.
updateManualUnsupported: Automatic updates are not supported on this system. Download the update manually.
updateFailedNetwork: Couldn't reach the update server. Check your network and try again.
updateFailedVerify: The downloaded update failed verification and was discarded.
updateFailedStorage: Couldn't save the update package (disk full or no permission).
updateFailedInstall: Installing the update failed. The current version is unchanged.
updateFailedElevationCancelled: Authorization was cancelled, so the update wasn't installed.
updateFailedIncomplete: The last update didn't finish installing. Try again or download it manually.
logExportDesc: Export logs to attach when submitting feedback
logStatusDegraded: App log writer degraded ({count} failure(s)). Last error: {error}
uploadTooLarge: The file is too large to upload
logMaxSizeDesc: Oldest logs are cleaned automatically when total size exceeds the limit
changelogSubtitle: FluxDown v{v} is out. Here's what's new:
feedbackDesc: Share your thoughts to help improve FluxDown
feedbackContactHint: Enter your email to receive progress notifications. Other contact methods may not receive notifications.
feedbackSysInfoHint: The app version and system info above are sent with your feedback to help diagnose issues. No personal or sensitive data is included.
feedbackAttachLogsHint: Include today's logs (sanitized) to help us diagnose the issue faster
feedbackError: Submission failed, please try again later
feedbackRateLimited: Too many requests, please try again later
hlsQualityDesc: Multiple quality options detected. Choose the one to download
resolveVariantDesc: Multiple download formats detected. Choose the one to download
pluginChoiceDesc: {count} plugins can handle links from {site}. Choose the one to use for this download
pluginChoiceRememberHint: You can change this later under Plugins → Site default plugins
pluginSiteDefaultsDesc: When several plugins can handle the same site, downloads use the plugin chosen here. Remove an entry to be asked again
pluginSiteDefaultAutomaticHint: Unattended downloads (silent mode, RSS, remote dispatch) picked this plugin automatically. Confirm it so regular downloads stop asking
pluginSiteDefaultSaveFailed: Failed to update the site default plugin: {error}
newDownloadCaptureContextHint: Links captured from the browser keep the original request's cookies, headers and referrer; values entered below take precedence
newDownloadCaptureAuthHint: The browser request already carries HTTP authentication and will be reused; enter a username here to use these credentials instead
closeWithActiveTasksHint: Exiting pauses all active downloads; they can resume the next time FluxDown starts.
mobileFileNotFound: File not found — it may have been moved or deleted
iosEmptyDownloadsSub: Add a link, magnet or torrent to start.
iosRssEmptySub: Follow an RSS or Atom feed and download new items automatically by your rules.
mobileLanguageSystemHint: The display language is set per app in the iOS Settings app.
mobileSaveDirIosFixed: Downloads are saved in the FluxDown folder of the Files app. iOS keeps this location fixed.
mobileLicenseEngineDepsDesc: The download engine is built from open-source Rust crates, each under its own license.
mobileNoAppToOpen: No app can open this file
mobileFooter: FluxDown · No ads · No tracking · Local-first
mobilePickDirUnmappable: Couldn't resolve the folder; pick one on device storage
mobileAllFilesDesc: Saving to public folders (e.g. Download) requires the "All files access" permission. Tap "Grant" to enable it in system settings.
fgServiceChannelDesc: Keeps downloads running while the app is in the background.
deleteConfirmDescWithFile: Delete "{fileName}" and its downloaded file? This cannot be undone.
deleteConfirmDescKeepFile: Delete "{fileName}"? The downloaded file will be kept on disk.
batchDeleteConfirmDescWithFile: Delete {count} selected tasks and their files? This cannot be undone.
batchDeleteConfirmDescKeepFile: Delete {count} selected tasks? Downloaded files will be kept on disk.
pluginLoadErrorBody: The plugin is installed, but FluxDown could not load it. Details:
pluginWindowLoadFailed: The plugin interface failed to load
pluginErrorMarketUnreachable: Can't reach the plugin marketplace. Check your network or proxy settings.
pluginErrorMarketIndexInvalid: The plugin marketplace index is malformed. Refresh later and try again.
pluginErrorMarketIndexRollback: The marketplace index is older than the last one seen and was rejected (possible tampering).
pluginErrorNotInMarket: This plugin is no longer listed in the marketplace.
pluginErrorYanked: The publisher has withdrawn this plugin version.
pluginErrorDownloadFailed: Couldn't download or verify the plugin package. Check your network and proxy settings, then try again. See the diagnostics log for details.
pluginErrorPackageTooLarge: The plugin package exceeds the 10 MB size limit.
pluginErrorPackageInvalid: Invalid plugin package: the manifest, script, or version check failed. See the diagnostics log for details.
pluginErrorMarketVersionChanged: The plugin was updated in the marketplace. Review its permissions and install again.
pluginDepsMissingBody: The plugin was installed, but its declared capabilities depend on components that are not installed yet: {components}. Those features stay unavailable until the components are set up. Go to component settings now?
pluginPermConfirmInstallBody: v{version} will be granted the following permissions:
pluginPermConfirmUpdateBody: v{version} requests permissions the installed version does not have:
pluginDetailSettingsCount: {count} field(s), configurable from the plugin card after install
pluginPermFfmpegDesc: Runs FFmpeg for audio/video processing (mux/transcode); requires the FFmpeg component
pluginPermYtdlpDesc: Runs yt-dlp to extract direct media URLs; requires the yt-dlp and FFmpeg components
pluginPermAuthDesc: Stores and reuses this plugin's site credentials, including cookies, Basic, bearer, or custom headers
pluginPermUnknownDesc: Unknown permission (not supported by this version)
pluginPermTasksDesc: Lists, creates, pauses, resumes and deletes download tasks
pluginPermBrowserRulesDesc: Contributes media sniffing rules to the browser extension
pluginPermDesktopDesc: Runs desktop scripts that can access local files, processes and network without restriction
pluginPermBackgroundDesc: Keeps the plugin running in the background even when no window is open
pluginPermInterceptDesc: Read and change the URL, request headers, cookies and body of matching tasks, renew their credentials mid-download, control their connection count, pick streaming quality, filter or re-sign streaming segments, request retries after failure and process files before completion.
pluginPermPageScriptsDesc: Runs the plugin's scripts on the websites listed below. Those scripts can read and modify the page content and your logged-in session on those sites.
pluginPermArchiveDesc: Reads file names and source-provided creator, series or collection information to choose an archive subfolder. It cannot access files, the network, other tasks or processes.
pluginRiskTooltipStandard: Only basic capabilities; cannot touch your tasks, credentials or local system
pluginRiskTooltipElevated: Can use components, credentials, tasks, browser rules, intercept downloads or run in the background
pluginRiskTooltipFull: Runs desktop scripts with unrestricted file, process and network access; install only from sources you trust
pluginConsentIntro: This plugin requests the following capabilities. It stays disabled until you grant them:
pluginConsentFullTrustWarning: This plugin runs with full trust. Its desktop scripts can read and write any file, start any process and access any network address, with your user privileges.
pluginConsentNativeNotAudited: Audit logs record only authorization, loading and fluxdown.* calls. Native file, process and network operations are not logged individually.
pluginViewDesktopOnly: This view is only available in the desktop app
pluginDetailUsageBody: Plugins are enabled by default after install and can be toggled in the Installed list at any time. Resolver plugins run automatically before matching downloads start — no manual action needed. Plugins with settings can be configured via the gear button on their card. A plugin that keeps failing is auto-disabled by the circuit breaker. Visit the plugin homepage for detailed usage.
privatePluginsSignInHint: Sign in to see plugins provisioned for you
privatePluginReplaceWarning: This private plugin will replace the plugin with the same ID already installed on this device.
pluginAuthDescription: The plugin drives QR-code login. Scan with the platform app and the system checks the login state automatically.
pluginAuthInputPlaceholder: Account, verification code, or other requested input
pluginAuthSuccess: Login successful; credentials will be reused until they expire
pluginAuthInvalidResponse: The plugin returned an invalid login response
pluginHelperScriptCopied: Script copied. Paste and run it in the site's DevTools console
taskIgnorePluginRetryMsg: This task failed while a plugin was resolving it. Ignoring will skip the plugin and retry with the original link directly. If this keeps happening, check the plugin's settings under Settings → Extensions → Plugins.
pluginAutoDisabledToast: Plugin "{name}" was auto-disabled after repeated failures. Re-enable it from Settings → Extensions → Plugins.
pluginRevokedToast: Plugin "{name}" was revoked by the plugin marketplace and has been disabled. Update it to re-enable.
duplicateTorrentToast: This torrent is already in task "{name}" — not added again
duplicateTorrentToastUnnamed: This torrent already exists in another task — not added again
componentsFfmpegDesc: Open-source audio/video toolkit. FluxDown uses it to merge separate audio and video tracks from DASH and similar streaming downloads.
componentsYtdlpDesc: Media extractor. FluxDown plugins use it to pull direct media URLs from 1000+ sites (YouTube, etc.) for the download engine.
componentsStatusNotFound: {name} not found. Install it below or specify a path manually.
componentsStatusNotFoundUnsupported: {name} not found. Add it to your system PATH or specify a path manually below.
componentsManagedUnsupported: Managed install isn't available on this platform (e.g. Alpine/OpenWrt musl libc). Use a {name} from your system package manager / PATH, or set a manual path above.
componentsManualPathDesc: Point directly to a {name} executable; takes priority over the managed install and system PATH.
componentsInstallSectionDescFfmpeg: Downloads a static FFmpeg build from the official BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds release on demand — not bundled with the installer.
componentsInstallSectionDescYtdlp: Downloads the official platform binary from the yt-dlp/yt-dlp GitHub release on demand — not bundled with the installer.
componentsUninstallConfirmMsg: This removes the managed {name} build. Manual and system-PATH {name} are not affected.
seedLocalDesc: Create a torrent for files or folders already on disk and start seeding them, no download needed.
seedLocalPathPlaceholder: Absolute path on the host running FluxDown
seedLocalTorrentHint: Leave empty to generate a torrent for the selected content. An existing .torrent must match the selected content.
seedLocalTrackersHint: One announce URL per line, written into the torrent. Shared magnet links also include the trackers from Settings › BitTorrent.
seedLocalUnlimitedDesc: Ignore share ratio, seeding time and inactive time limits until you stop it manually.
seedLocalWorking: Creating the torrent and verifying data. Large files can take several minutes.
seedLocalErrPathRequired: Choose the file or folder to seed
btNoTorrentFile: This task has no .torrent file (magnet-only task). Copy the magnet link instead.
btTrackersEmpty: No trackers. Peers are found through DHT / PEX only.
btTrackersNoneWorking: No tracker has answered yet, so other people may not find you. Check your network, proxy and port forwarding.
btTrackerSourceTorrentHint: Included in the torrent or magnet link
btTrackerSourceSessionHint: Added from your settings (custom, built-in public or subscribed tracker list); not part of the torrent
btPeersIdleHint: The task is not running, so no peers are connected.
btSeedMaxActiveDesc: Maximum number of tasks seeding at the same time (0 = unlimited). Completed tasks beyond the limit are queued for seeding.
btAutoReseedDesc: Automatically continue seeding completed tasks after restart, unless seeding was stopped manually
btSeedEnabledDesc: Automatically start seeding when a BT task finishes downloading. Turn off to stop seeding immediately upon completion. Seeding keeps the disk awake, which may stop a NAS or external drive from sleeping
btSeedUploadLimitHint: Upload limit takes effect the next time the task starts or seeding is remounted
manifestTreeEmpty: No matching files — adjust the filter or search
manifestAdvancedHint: Proxy · UA · cookies · headers · threads — group-level, applied to every sub-task
manifestProxyHint: Leave blank to use the global setting
manifestIgnoreTlsHint: Accepts expired or self-signed certificates for this group's sub-tasks only; downloads may be exposed to man-in-the-middle interception.
manifestCookieHint: Usually required for cloud-drive logins (leave blank to send none)
manifestHeadersHint: Extra HTTP headers applied to the whole group (use the Cookie field above for cookies)
groupMemberExpiredResolve: Direct link expired · will re-resolve automatically on next launch ↻
groupDetailLazyRenewHint: Lazy renewal: link re-resolves automatically on every launch
showSidebarRssDesc: Show the RSS subscriptions section in the sidebar
rssSidebarEmptyHint: No subscriptions yet — click + and paste a feed URL.
rssInvalidNumber: Enter a valid number within the allowed range.
rssInvalidSizeRange: Maximum size cannot be smaller than minimum size.
rssValidateBeforeSave: Verify the current feed before subscribing.
rssEditorAuthHint: For feeds requiring cookies or a proxy, configure them under Advanced before verifying.
rssDeleteConfirmDesc: Delete "{name}"? Its item history is removed, but downloads already created are kept.
rssEmptyDesc: Items from the first fetch are marked as read; only items appearing afterwards are downloaded automatically.
rssEmptyFetchingHint: Running the first fetch. This usually takes a few seconds; slow origins or proxied feeds take longer.
rssEmptyErrorHint: The fetch did not complete. Check that the feed URL is reachable; sites that require a login need a cookie under Advanced, and unreachable hosts need a dedicated proxy.
rssNameHint: Leave empty to use the feed title
rssIntervalHint: Fetches that find new items write to disk and may wake a sleeping NAS drive; use a longer interval if that matters
rssProviderPluginHint: This source will be fetched by the selected plugin. Configure the plugin under Settings > Plugins; no extra subscription entry is required.
rssProviderUnavailable: The plugin that provides "{id}" is not installed, is disabled or still needs authorisation. This source cannot fetch until it is available again.
rssProviderConfigHint: Optional. Passed to the plugin unchanged; see the plugin's documentation for what it accepts. Leave empty if it needs none.
rssProviderConfigInvalid: Provider configuration must be empty or valid JSON.
rssEnabledDesc: Disabling keeps the settings and history but stops fetching.
rssAutoDownloadDesc: Off = collect only: items are listed for you to pick by hand.
rssStartPausedDesc: Tasks are created but do not start, so they take no concurrency slot.
rssUseRegexDesc: Include/exclude are parsed as Rust regex. An invalid pattern lets everything through.
rssSmartEpisodeDesc: Recognises S01E02 / 1x02 / - 02 / 第02话 and keeps one release per episode. Unrecognised titles pass through.
rssPreviewHeader: Rule preview — live against {n} cached item(s)
rssPreviewEmpty: No cached items yet — fetch once to preview the rules.
rssSendRefererDesc: Attaches the feed site as Referer; some private trackers require it.
rssNotifyDesc: One batched notification per fetch, not one per item.
rssWizardStep2: Step 2 of 2 — where do the downloads go?
rssWizardUrlNote: Private feeds with a token in the URL work as-is. Feeds needing cookies can be configured afterwards under Manage subscription · Advanced.
rssWizardSeedNote: Items already in the feed are marked as read; only items published after subscribing are downloaded automatically.
soundGroupDesc: Play a sound on this device when downloads start, finish or fail
soundTaskCompletedDesc: When a download finishes; replaces the system notification sound
soundQueueFinishedDesc: When every task in a queue is done
soundErrorUnplayable: Can't play this sound. Check that the file exists and is a supported audio file.
soundErrorUnavailable: Sound playback isn't available on this device.
soundErrorInvalidFile: Unsupported file type. Choose a {formats} file.
soundErrorInvalidPath: This file path can't be used as a sound.
webhookEmptyDesc: Send HTTP notifications to your services when download events happen.
webhookDialogDesc: Task events are pushed to your endpoint over HTTP POST — pick a service preset and the payload format is generated for you.
webhookUrlHint: Paste the push URL the service gave you
webhookUrlHintNtfy: The URL must include the topic path, e.g. https://ntfy.sh/my-topic
webhookUrlHintDingtalk: In the DingTalk bot's security settings choose "Custom keywords" and add FluxDown, otherwise messages are rejected
webhookUrlWarnHttp: Plaintext HTTP — turn on “Allow plaintext HTTP” under Advanced
webhookUrlInvalid: This is not a valid http(s) URL
webhookEventsEmpty: No events selected — this endpoint will never fire
webhookTemplateHint: Leave empty to use the preset default. Placeholder substitution only — no conditions, no loops.
webhookSignDesc: Adds an X-FluxDown-Signature header (t=timestamp,v1=digest) so the receiver can verify origin and reject replays.
webhookAllowHttpDesc: Only recommended for LAN devices (Home Assistant, NAS…).
webhookUseProxyDesc: Off by default — forcing a LAN endpoint through a proxy always fails. Turn it on for services that need one (Telegram, Discord…).

Any 2xx = success · 10s timeout per attempt
Network errors and 5xx retry 3× (2s/4s/8s)
4xx is not retried (treated as a config error)
Deliveries to one endpoint are serialised, preserving order
webhookLogSimulateHint: Pushes a sample event through each endpoint’s real subscription rules — no actual download needed.
webhookLogHint4xx: 4xx is treated as a configuration error and is not retried — check whether the webhook still exists on the server.
webhookSimulateNoTarget: No target subscribes to task.completed — nothing was sent.
webhookSimulateDispatched: Queued for {n} endpoint(s). Delivery results will appear in the log.
pushNavDesc: Get notified on your phone, inbox or group chat when downloads finish or fail
webhookEmptyDescSelfHosted: Push straight from this device to ntfy, Bark, WeCom / Feishu / DingTalk groups, Telegram, Discord, or self-hosted services like Home Assistant and a NAS
cloudNotifySignedOutTitle: Sign in to FluxCloud to get download alerts on your phone
cloudNotifySignedOutDesc: Set it up once — every signed-in device pushes to the same channels.
cloudNotifyReportDesc: When on, download events from this device are sent to FluxCloud, which pushes them to your channels.
cloudNotifyPrivacyDesc: File name, size and status are always sent. Download URL and save location may be sensitive and are off by default.
cloudNotifyConsentDesc: Download events from this device (file name, size, status) will be sent to FluxCloud to deliver notifications and deleted after 7 days. This is separate from anonymous usage statistics and can be turned off anytime.
cloudNotifyPlanDisabled: Your plan doesn't include cloud push
cloudNotifyChannelsDesc: Set up once, shared by all signed-in devices
cloudNotifyEmailExists: That address is already in the list
cloudNotifyKindEmailDesc: Delivered to your inbox — up to 5 recipients per channel

doctorCopied: Report copied — paste it straight into your feedback

doctorNmhLogEmpty: No relay log yet — the browser extension has never connected

doctorHintReregisterNmh: Hit “Re-register” on this row, then restart your browser
doctorHintNmhOtherInstall: The extension works: another FluxDown installation serves it, and a browser cold start launches that installation. Hit “Use this installation” to switch
doctorHintRestartApp: Hit “Restart listener” on this row; if it still fails, restart FluxDown
doctorHintEnableLocalServer: Hit “Enable service” on this row, or turn it on under Settings › API Service
doctorHintCheckFirewall: Check whether a firewall or security suite is blocking the local port
doctorHintEnableProtocol: Hit “Register” on this row, or enable the association under Settings › General
doctorHintProtocolClaimed: Another app owns this protocol — hit “Register” on this row to take it back
doctorHintAssociationOff: Turned off under Settings › General. No other app on this system can take it over, so the system still hands it to FluxDown, which ignores it
doctorHintCheckDisk: Check free disk space and write permissions on the folder
doctorListenerRestartOk: Local listener restarted — reconnect from the browser extension
autoResumeOnStartDesc: Automatically continue tasks that were downloading when the app was last closed
localServiceInvalidArgument: The value was rejected by the local service
apiServiceLanRestartHint: Takes effect the next time the local service starts
webLogoutDesc: Clears the access key saved in this browser, disconnects, and returns to the sign-in page.
btMseModeDesc: Disabled: plaintext only · Enabled: prefer encrypted, accept plaintext · Forced: encrypted peers only
doctorHintDaemonStartupFailed: The download daemon keeps exiting right after launch — usually its local port (17801) is unavailable or another process holds the data directory. Check the stderr excerpt above and fluxdownd.stderr.log, then restart FluxDown
doctorHintDiskSleepBlockers: Seeding, RSS auto-fetch and idle file scan keep touching the disk while idle, which can stop a NAS disk from spinning down. Pause or stop seeding, disable or lengthen RSS sources, or turn idle file scan off if you want the disk to sleep
doctorHintDirPermission: FluxDown cannot write to this folder. Click "Fix permissions" to give write access back to the current user (if the folder belongs to another user, administrator authorization is requested and only this folder is changed). Without that button (for example Docker / NAS), check the folder owner and permissions; for Docker, check PUID/PGID and the volume mount. If it still fails on Windows, Controlled Folder Access may be blocking it: allow FluxDown in Windows Security
doctorHintDirPermissionMacos: macOS privacy protection blocked the write. Click "Open System Settings" and allow FluxDown in Privacy & Security › Files and Folders (other locations need Full Disk Access), then run the diagnostics again
doctorHintDirReadOnly: The disk holding this folder is mounted read-only. Remount it read-write or choose another folder
doctorHintLowDiskSpace: Not enough free space: large files and BT tasks will fail. Free up space or choose a folder on a larger disk
doctorHintDirMissing: Neither the folder nor its parents exist. Make sure the external or network drive is connected, or choose the folder again in Settings
doctorHintDirTimeout: The disk did not respond in time. Check the network drive connection or the disk's health
doctorHintComponentBlocked: The system refused to run this program. Check its execute permission and mount options (noexec); on macOS remove the quarantine attribute or allow it in Privacy & Security; on Windows check whether security software blocks it; or reinstall it in Settings › Components
doctorHintComponentBlockedFixable: The system refused to run this component installed by FluxDown. Click "Fix execute permission"; if it still fails, the data folder may be mounted with noexec or security software may block it — reinstall it in Settings › Components
doctorHintPermissionProbeFailed: The download service did not finish the folder and component checks in time. Restart FluxDown and run the diagnostics again
doctorHintComponentBroken: The program starts but fails (corrupted file, wrong architecture or missing libraries). Reinstall it or pick another version in Settings › Components
doctorHintAutostartBlocked: Launch at startup is disabled by the system. Click "Re-enable" to restore it; if that does not help, enable it in Windows Settings › Apps › Startup or Task Manager, in macOS System Settings › General › Login Items, or in your desktop environment's autostart settings
doctorHintNotificationsBlocked: The system has turned off FluxDown notifications. Click "Open System Settings", allow FluxDown in the notification settings, then run the diagnostics again
doctorHintNotificationsUnavailable: This session has no notification service (no notification daemon is running), so download notifications will not appear
doctorHintNotificationsUnverified: The system does not expose notification permission. Click "Send test notification"; if nothing appears, allow "Script Editor" in System Settings › Notifications
doctorTestNotificationBody: If you can see this, download notifications work.
doctorHintNmhLaunchFailed: Launching the relay the way a browser does failed, so the browser extension cannot connect. Click "Re-register" to rewrite the registration (administrator authorization is requested if old files must be given back to you); if it still fails, check security software or reinstall FluxDown
doctorHintNmhPolicyBlocked: An organization policy (NativeMessagingBlocklist) blocks FluxDown's native messaging host. This is an administrator setting that FluxDown does not bypass; ask IT to allow com.fluxdown.nmh
doctorHintNmhUserHostsDisabled: An organization policy (NativeMessagingUserLevelHosts) disables per-user native messaging hosts, so the browser ignores FluxDown's registration. This is an administrator setting that FluxDown does not bypass; contact IT
doctorHintNmhCmdDisabled: A group policy (DisableCMD) turns off the command prompt, which Chrome / Edge use to start native messaging hosts, so the extension cannot connect. Ask your administrator to set the policy to "No" or to allow scripts
doctorHintNmhForeignOwned: These files belong to another user (usually because FluxDown was once run with sudo), so the registration can no longer be updated automatically. Click "Re-register" and authorize to give them back to the current user
doctorHintNmhComspecInvalid: The Windows environment variable ComSpec does not point to the command prompt (cmd.exe). Chrome / Edge start native messaging hosts through it, so the extension cannot connect. Click "Fix ComSpec" to restore %SystemRoot%\system32\cmd.exe (no administrator rights needed), then fully exit the browser (including its system tray icon) and open it again
doctorHintNmhComspecRestart: ComSpec is correct now, but programs started before the change keep the old value until they restart — FluxDown included, and most likely your browser. Fully exit the browser (including its system tray icon; chrome://restart is not enough) and open it again from the Start menu or taskbar. If the extension still cannot connect, click "Fix ComSpec" to notify Windows again, or sign out and back in. This notice disappears once FluxDown restarts
doctorComspecFixed: ComSpec fixed. Programs that are already running keep the old value: fully exit the browser (including its system tray icon) and open it again; if the extension still cannot connect, sign out of Windows and back in
doctorHintRunningElevated: FluxDown is running as root, so every file it writes belongs to root and cannot be changed later by your normal account. Restart FluxDown as your normal user
doctorHintRunningAsAdmin: FluxDown is running as administrator, so the browser extension cannot connect to it and files it opens also run as administrator. Quit FluxDown from the tray, then start it normally (not with "Run as administrator")
doctorRepairCancelled: Authorization was cancelled; the changes that needed it were not made
doctorRepairUnavailable: Administrator authorization could not be requested (for example, no polkit authentication agent). Follow the hint for this item to fix it manually
doctorRepairRunningElevated: FluxDown is running as root, so permissions cannot be given back to a normal user. Restart FluxDown as your normal user, then repair
doctorRepairIncomplete: The repair ran, but the check still fails. Follow the hint for this item to continue
doctorRepairNotApplicable: This item cannot be repaired automatically (for example, a system folder or the home folder itself). Follow the hint or choose another folder
doctorTestNotificationSent: Test notification sent; if you did not see it, check the system notification settings
doctorSettingsOpened: System Settings opened; run the diagnostics again after changing it

errReasonMailNotConfigured: The server can't send email right now. Contact the administrator.

errReasonPairingCodeInvalid: The pairing code is wrong or has expired.
errReasonPairingTimeout: The other device didn't confirm in time. Start again and approve the request on that device.
errReasonPeerClockSkew: The two devices' clocks differ too much. Turn on automatic date & time on both devices and try again.
errReasonPairingSessionExpired: The pairing session has expired. Start again.
errReasonPairingPeerUnreachable: Can't reach that address. Check the address, that both devices are online, and that the target device has Settings → API service → Allow LAN / VPN access turned on.
errReasonPairingNotFluxDown: That address isn't a FluxDown service. Check the protocol, port or reverse proxy.
errReasonPairingThrottled: Too many failed attempts. Try again later.
errReasonPairingRejected: The other device rejected the pairing.
errReasonPairingSignatureInvalid: The other device's identity check failed.
errReasonPairingSelf: A device can't pair with itself.
errReasonPairingVersionMismatch: The other device uses an incompatible pairing protocol. Update both devices to the same FluxDown version.
errReasonPeerNotPaired: That device isn't paired (or was unpaired).
localPairingMyCodeHint: Enter this code (and address) on the other device to pair with this one.
localPairingNoAddress: No LAN address is available for this device.
localPairingLanDisabledHint: LAN access is off, so other devices can't find or reach this one. Turn on Allow LAN / VPN access under Settings → API service, then restart FluxDown.
localPairingAddressHint: host, host:port, or http(s)://host[:port][/path]. Defaults: http 17800, https 443.

accountErrorDeviceUntrusted: This device is no longer trusted for this account. Please sign in again.
localPairingAddressInvalid: Enter a valid address: host, host:port or http(s)://host[:port]
localPairingLanRestartHint: LAN access is on. Restart FluxDown (tray menu → Restart) for it to take effect.
localPairingOneWayHint: LAN access is off on this device: after pairing, only this device can send downloads to the other one, not the other way round.
linkedDeviceRenameHint: Only shown on this device. Leave empty to use the other device's own name.
linkedDeviceRevokedDesc: The other device removed this pairing, so you can no longer send downloads to it. Remove it and pair again if needed.
linkDispatchedToDevice: Sent to {device}. Check download progress on that device.

mobileHostErrIncompatible: This host runs an incompatible FluxDown version. Update FluxDown on the host.

mobileHostAddressHint: host, host:port or http(s)://host[:port]; default port 17800 (443 for https)

mobileHostKeyHint: {min}–{max} printable ASCII characters with letters and digits
mobileDlNotifChannelDesc: Shown while downloads run on this phone so they keep going in the background
mobileNotifSystemFooterAndroid: Completion notifications follow your signed-in devices; the other switches apply to this phone only. Notifications are shown for the host you are viewing and for downloads on this phone.
mobileSaveDirNotWritable: Can't write to "{dir}". Check storage access and whether the folder is read-only. Android still protects other apps' private folders.
mobileAllFilesDescNative: Android requires "All files access" for FluxDown to open and save to this location. Turn it on in system settings; the folder reloads when you come back. The app folder works without it.
mobileStoragePermDesc: Android 10 and earlier require the storage permission for FluxDown to open and save to this location. The folder reloads once you grant it. The app folder works without it.
mobileLocalFolderReadFailed: Couldn't open this folder. It may have been removed, or the storage is unavailable.
mobileLocalFolderAppDirDesc: No permission needed · removed when FluxDown is uninstalled
mobileLocalFolderProtected: Android protects this folder. No app can save files here; choose another location.
mobileLocalFolderTimeout: "{dir}" isn't responding. Check that the storage is still connected and try again.
mobileLocalFolderMissing: That folder doesn't exist yet; showing its nearest parent. Use New folder to create it.
mobileLocalFolderEmptyHint: Save here, or create a new folder.
mobileLocalFolderCreateFailed: Couldn't create "{name}". A file with that name may exist, or this location is read-only.
mobileAddDeviceForeground: Keep this page open until both devices have confirmed.
mobileAddDeviceNoGatewayHint: This phone has no network service other devices can connect to. To pair, enter the other device's address and pairing code below.
mobileAddHostPairIntro: On the host, open Settings → Account → Add device to show a pairing code, then pick the host below and enter the code.
mobileAddHostNoneFound: No hosts found. Make sure the host is showing a pairing code, or enter its address.
mobileAddHostVerifyHint: Make sure the host shows the same number, then approve the request on the host.
mobileAddHostWaitingApproval: Waiting for the host to approve…
mobileAddHostControlUnsupported: This host is too old for LAN pairing. Update FluxDown on the host or use an access key.
mobileHostRepairNeeded: This phone's access to the host was revoked. Pair again to reconnect.

linkControlPairCodeHint: To control this FluxDown from a phone, choose Add host → LAN pairing on the phone and enter this code.

mobileDeviceGone: This device is no longer available
mobileDevicesLoginGuide: Sign in to send downloads between your devices
mobileDispatchFileNameSingleOnly: A file name can only be set when sending a single link.
mobileDispatchUrlsHint: One link per line. Each link becomes its own task on the target device.
mobileIncomingPairingCancelled: The pairing request was cancelled or has expired.

mobileRemoteTasksEmpty: No downloads sent to other devices yet

mobileRemoteTasksNoMatch: No remote tasks match this filter.

apiServiceTokenRevealAuth: Authenticate to view or copy the access token
mobileApiForgetHostDesc: Removes this host and its saved access key from this device, then switches back to this iPhone. The host itself is not changed.
mobileGroupGoneSub: It may have been deleted. Go back to the list.
torrentImportTooLarge: “{name}” is larger than 4 MiB, which is more than a torrent file can be.
manifestNoItems: The plugin didn't return a file list for this link.
manifestResolveTimedOut: Checking took too long. Check the network or login state and try again.
taskIgnorePluginRetryDone: Plugin ignored, retrying with the original link
mobileRssSelectFeedHint: Choose a subscription to see its items.
btMobileFootnote: iOS limits background time. Seeding and UPnP port mapping only work while the app is in the foreground or running a background task.
btPortRangeInvalid: The end port must not be lower than the start port.
btMseModeDisabledDesc: Plaintext only. Never use protocol encryption.

btMseModeForcedDesc: Only connect to peers that support encryption.
settingsSyncLegend: The cloud icon marks settings that sync across your signed-in devices.
mobileFolderDenied: The service has no permission to read this folder
mobileGeneralBgContinueDesc: Keeps active downloads running in the background for as long as iOS allows.
bgDownloadFootnote: iOS limits how long apps can run in the background. The system may pause downloads at any time; they resume automatically when you return to the app.
mobileGeneralKeepAwakeDesc: Keeps the screen from locking while downloads are active and FluxDown is open.
mobileGeneralLinkHandlingDesc: The links and files FluxDown is set up to open. iOS picks the default app, so FluxDown cannot tell whether another app takes precedence.
mobileGeneralDownloadsViewFooter: Controls which sections appear in the Downloads filter bar and, on iPad, in the sidebar.
mobileGeneralEntriesFooter: Choose which entries appear in the tab bar and menus. Downloads, Devices and Settings are always shown.
mobileGeneralAutoDirsNeedDefault: Set a default save location first.
mobileGeneralAutoDirsUnchanged: Category folders are already up to date
mobileSiteAuthRemoteNote: These credentials are stored on “{host}”, not on this phone.

mobileNotifFileConflictBody: “{name}” already exists. Tap to choose what to do
mobileNotifPermAskDetail: Allow notifications to hear when downloads finish, fail or need your choice.
mobileNotifPermOnDetail: FluxDown can tell you when downloads finish or fail.
mobileNotifPermQuietDetail: They appear in Notification Center without banners or sounds.
mobileNotifPermDeniedDetail: Turn on notifications for FluxDown in Settings to get download alerts.
mobileNotifActionsDesc: Add Open and Share buttons to completion notifications. Share is offered for files stored on this phone.
mobileNotifOnFailureDesc: Tell me when a download fails.
mobileNotifSelectionDesc: When a download needs a choice (BT files, video quality, a file that already exists) while FluxDown isn't on screen, you get a notification. Tap it to choose, or use its Use default button.
mobileNotifSystemFooter: Completion notifications follow your signed-in devices; the other switches apply to this phone only. Notifications are shown for the host you are viewing.
mobileNotifWebhookDesc: Push task events to your own server, chat bot or automation.

mobileDiagHostNotRun: Run diagnostics to check this host.
mobileDiagNotifQuietHint: Notifications reach Notification Center without banners or sounds. Open Settings › Notifications to allow banners.
mobileDiagNotifUnaskedHint: Open Settings › Notifications in FluxDown and tap Allow notifications.
mobileDiagNotifDeniedHint: Allow notifications for FluxDown in Settings to be told when downloads finish or fail.
mobileDiagBgContinueOffHint: Downloads on this phone pause when you leave FluxDown. Turn it on in General settings.
mobileDiagBgRefreshOffHint: Background App Refresh is off for FluxDown. Turn it on in Settings so iOS can keep downloads running in the background.
mobileDiagBgLowPowerHint: Low Power Mode limits background activity, so downloads may pause when you leave FluxDown.
mobileDiagStorageNotWritable: Can't write to the Downloads folder
mobileDiagStorageNotWritableHint: FluxDown can't create files in its folder. Free up space or restart the app; if it persists, reinstall FluxDown.
mobileDiagStorageLowHint: Free space is low: large files and BT tasks will fail. Delete files or offload apps in Settings › General › iPhone Storage.
mobileDiagLinksHint: This build doesn't declare the link handler, so magnet and ed2k links won't open FluxDown. Reinstall FluxDown.

mobileDiagNetMeteredHint: This connection may be metered. Large downloads can use your data plan.
mobileDiagNetLowDataHint: Low Data Mode asks apps to use less data and can slow downloads. Turn it off in the network's settings.
mobileDiagLocalNetDetail: Needed to reach hosts and paired devices on your Wi-Fi. iOS doesn't report the status.
mobileDiagLocalNetHint: If a host on your local network can't be reached, check Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network and allow FluxDown.
mobileDiagEngineStaleHint: The connection to the download engine dropped and is being restored. Settings and actions are read-only meanwhile.
mobileDiagEngineFailedHint: Check that the host is online and its address and access key are correct, or switch to this phone.
mobileLogExportCleartext: iOS blocks plain-HTTP downloads from this host. Use an https address to export logs.
mobileComponentMirrorBaseDesc: Optional HTTPS base URL of a GitHub release mirror used when downloading FFmpeg and yt-dlp. Leave empty to download directly.
mobileBtAndroidFootnote: Android may suspend background network activity. Seeding and UPnP port mapping work most reliably while the app is open or the download service is running.
mobileEd2kNodesDatUrlDesc: Where to download the Kad bootstrap node list (nodes.dat). Leave empty to use the built-in default
mobileGeneralBgFootnote: Downloads on this phone keep running in the background behind an ongoing notification. Some manufacturers aggressively limit background apps; if downloads stall with the screen off, exempt FluxDown from battery optimization.
mobileGeneralBatteryOptDesc: Exempt FluxDown from battery optimization so the system doesn't interrupt downloads while the screen is off.
mobileGeneralLinkHandlingDescAndroid: The links FluxDown is set up to open. Android lets you choose the default app for each link type, so another app may still take precedence.
mobileGeneralOpenByDefaultDesc: Open Android's default-app settings for FluxDown.
mobileGeneralDownloadsViewFooterAndroid: Controls which sections appear in the Downloads filter bar and, on tablets, in the side rail.
mobileNotifSelectionDescAndroid: When a download needs a choice (BT files, video quality, a file that already exists) while FluxDown isn't on screen, you get a notification. Tap it to choose.
mobileDiagAndNotifChannelOff: Some notification channels are turned off
mobileDiagAndNotifChannelOffHint: Open FluxDown's notification settings and turn the channels back on, otherwise download progress and results won't be shown.
mobileDiagAndBgRestrictedHint: Android stops FluxDown from running in the background, so downloads pause when you leave the app. Open App info › Battery and choose Unrestricted.
mobileDiagAndBgOptimizedHint: Downloads keep running through the notification, but Android may delay network access while the screen is off. Allow unrestricted battery usage for steadier background downloads.
mobileDiagAndBgPowerSaveHint: Battery Saver limits background network access, so downloads may stall when you leave FluxDown.
mobileDiagAndStorageLowHint: Free space is low: large files and BT tasks will fail. Delete files or move apps in Settings › Storage.
mobileDiagAndLinksHint: Another app, or no app, is set to open magnet / ed2k links. Clear the other app's defaults in its App info (Open by default), or pick FluxDown with “Always” the next time you tap a link.
mobileDiagAndNetNoInternet: Connected, but internet access isn't verified
mobileDiagAndNetNoInternetHint: The network may need a sign-in page or has no route to the internet. Check the connection or switch networks.
mobileDiagAndNetDataSaverHint: Data Saver restricts background data, which can pause downloads when you leave FluxDown. Allow unrestricted data for FluxDown.
mobileUpdateReady: v{v} is downloaded. Tap to install.
mobileUpdateManualStore: FluxDown was installed from an app store. Update it there, or download the package from the website.

settingsCatShortcutsDesc: Customize in-app and global keyboard shortcuts
shortcutAppDesc: Work while a FluxDown window is focused.
shortcutGlobalDesc: System-wide shortcuts handled by the background agent; they keep working after the window is closed.
shortcutRecordHint: Press a key combination, or double-tap {keys}
shortcutCrossScopeGlobal: The same key is also a global shortcut for “{action}”
shortcutCrossScopeApp: The same key is also an in-app shortcut for “{action}”
shortcutErrorGlobalNeedsModifier: Global shortcuts need Ctrl, Alt or Win/⌘ (F1–F20 can be used alone)
shortcutErrorUnsupportedKey: This key cannot be used for shortcuts
shortcutErrorDoubleTapUnsupported: Double-tapping a modifier is not supported by this desktop environment
shortcutGlobalUnavailableDesc: The background agent cannot listen for system-wide keys in this environment (no graphical session or unsupported platform), so global shortcuts cannot be recorded.
shortcutWaylandDesc: On Wayland, global shortcuts go through the desktop's shortcut portal: the system asks you to confirm the final keys, and double-tapping a modifier is not supported.
shortcutPermissionDesc: macOS only lets apps listen for system-wide keys after you allow FluxDown in Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Shortcuts take effect once permission is granted.
btGuardEnabledDesc: Detect peers that only take from you or fake their progress, then observe, throttle, choke or block them. Applies to the whole BT engine and takes effect immediately
btGuardSessionOff: The BT engine is not running; protection starts together with it
btGuardSectionRulesDesc: Observe only records what a rule would do without touching the peer. Review the event log, then switch the rules you trust to Enforce
btGuardRuleExcessiveDesc: A peer group has downloaded far more from you than the whole torrent (repeated re-downloading)
btGuardRuleRerequestDesc: The peer asks for pieces it has already announced it owns
btGuardRuleRewindDesc: The peer reconnects reporting fewer pieces than before, to download the same data again
btGuardRuleLagDesc: Pieces you sent never show up in the peer's progress; the peer is probed with one disconnect
btGuardRuleFingerprintDesc: Client name or peer ID matches a known leech client from the cloud list. Never bans on its own
btGuardExcessRatioDesc: Trigger when a group has downloaded more than this share of the torrent size from you (100% = one full copy)
btGuardMinTorrentDesc: Smaller torrents never trigger the excessive-upload rule
btGuardRewindToleranceDesc: Share of previously held pieces a reconnecting peer may drop before it counts as a rewind
btGuardIpv6PrefixDesc: IPv6 peers are grouped by this prefix length, so rotating addresses inside one subnet count as one peer
btGuardThrottleKibDesc: Upload speed shared by all throttled peers combined
btGuardBanBaseHoursDesc: Each repeated strong offence multiplies the duration by 4
btGuardDownloadingMaxActionDesc: Strongest action applied to peers of tasks that are still downloading, so a wrong verdict cannot stall your own download
btGuardSkipPrivateDesc: Peers of private torrents are not inspected
btGuardSkipLanDesc: Exempt private-network, loopback, link-local and carrier-grade NAT addresses
btGuardCloudEnabledDesc: Fetch a signed blocklist from FluxCloud every few hours and verify it locally before use
btGuardCloudDisabled: The cloud blocklist is turned off
btGuardCloudNone: No blocklist has been loaded yet
btGuardCloudStale: Expired — the cloud layer is paused until a new list arrives
btGuardFilterUrlsDesc: Add IP blocklist links (e.g. ipfilter.dat). Listed IPs are refused outright. Updated every 24 hours
btGuardFilterUrlsPlaceholder:
One URL per line, e.g.:
https://example.com/blocklist.txt
btGuardReportEnabledDesc: Help build the community blocklist by reporting peers that trigger rules. Off by default and stored on this device only
btGuardReportLoginRequired: Sign in to your FluxDown account to turn on reporting
btGuardReportContents:
Sent: the offending peer's IP group, the rule that fired, byte counts and ratios, the client name or peer ID prefix, and the torrent's size and infohash.
Never sent: file names, paths, torrent names, or anything from private torrents.
FluxCloud hashes the infohash on arrival and does not keep the original. Reporting needs a signed-in account.
btGuardReportConsentBody:
When this is on, FluxDown uploads evidence about peers that trigger anti-leech rules so FluxCloud can build a shared blocklist.

Sent: the peer's IP group, the rule that fired, byte counts and ratios, the client name or peer ID prefix, the torrent size and infohash.
Never sent: file names, paths, torrent names, or private torrents.
FluxCloud hashes the infohash immediately and keeps no original.

You must be signed in, and you can turn this off at any time.
btGuardCloudEntryHint: Cloud entries can't be deleted. Allow-list the address instead.
btGuardAddTitle: Add a block or allow entry
btGuardErrCidrEmpty: Enter an IP address or CIDR range
btGuardErrCidrInvalid: Not a valid IP address or CIDR range
btGuardEvidenceNone: No stored evidence for this group yet
